facts.claim: A handled ascender, the jumar a climber slides up a fixed rope, weighs about this much.

versions.note: Petzl's ASCENSION handled ascender, by its specifications.

facts.claim: A technical ice tool, the second tool a climber carries beside their ice axe to climb steep ice, weighs about this much.

versions.note: Petzl's QUARK, with its adze or its hammer, its shaft 50 cm long.

facts.claim: A litre of water weighs a kilogram.

versions.note: A litre of liquid water has a mass of almost exactly one kilogram; the bottle is the climber's own load.

facts.claim: An energy bar, the food a climber eats on the move, weighs about this much.

versions.note: A Clif Bar, by its label.

source.title: Open Food Facts: Chocolate Chip – CLIF Bar

facts.claim: An energy bar gives about this much energy.

versions.note: A Clif Bar, a serving of one bar: 1,046 kJ.

source.title: Open Food Facts: Chocolate Chip – CLIF Bar

facts.claim: The most water a climber packs, in litres: two bottles in their insulated covers and a flask. A day on Everest takes more than that (body.water-loss), so the rest is drunk at the camps.
The most bars of food a climber packs for a day between two camps.
The most bottles of oxygen a climber carries themselves: each weighs as much as everything else in the pack together (oxygen.bottle-weight).
How much water a climber drinks when they stop for a drink, in litres: half a bottle.

facts.question: What does a client carry through the Icefall on a rotation to Camp 1, and what do they leave at Base Camp or have carried for them: how much water and food, a second ice tool, oxygen? What's cached at Camp 1?
